items.title: Exact score attribution and controlled ablation
items.summary: Audit explicit scoring computation: reconstruct contributions at frozen transforms, then ablate terms to test rank sensitivity; MEGADOCK exposes scoring variants and weights (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md). Diagnostic proposal written to interp.md.
items.root_link: Addresses dense-search best50 gains versus rank1 losses, without changing frozen replication arms: file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md.
items.sequential: Proposed audit needs baseline plus three ablations per case/arm across four cases and three arms; frozen-pose calculations split independently and CPU analysis uses zero GPU capacity. Full-search variants retain roughly five dependent stages per rotation across 3,600 or 54,000 rotations, but rotations already support concurrent OpenMP execution; instrumented GPU busy fraction remains unknown: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md.
items.narrowing: Score contributions explain algorithmic preference; leave timing, numerical acceptance and biological correctness to original protocol.

items.title: Differential tracing of CPU/GPU numerical disagreement
items.summary: Compare intermediate arrays to locate first divergence, then test independent numerical fixtures; reassociation and fused multiply-add can change compliant floating-point results (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/floating-point/index.html). Tracing supports diagnosis, not automatic acceptance.
items.root_link: Supports same-settings CPU/GPU agreement gate and independent tolerance justification: file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md.
items.sequential: Proposed minimum: eight instrumented executions, CPU/GPU pair per case, each with about six ordered checkpoints consuming preceding arrays; GPU acquisition reserves one device with unknown busy fraction, while stored-trace analysis uses zero GPU. Cases and rotations can run concurrently if memory, transfers and host capacity permit, while within-rotation dependencies remain; nearest demonstrated implementation distributes docking work: https://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/perform.html.
items.narrowing: First divergent intermediate identifies implementation cause; does not establish acceptable scientific error or complete-workflow speedup.

items.title: Protein-language-model SAE hypothesis audit
items.summary: Conditional Goodfire-style branch: inspect biological features, then intervene on activations; Goodfire reports preliminary Evo 2 steering, while InterPLM demonstrates localized protein-feature interventions (https://www.goodfire.com/research/interpreting-evo-2; https://arxiv.org/html/2412.12101v1). Proposed use: follow-up hypotheses.
items.root_link: Bears on biological hypotheses behind pose preference, leaving original acceleration, agreement and same-budget quality comparisons unresolved: file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md.
items.compute_open: More parallel compute buys features and layers analysed; cited InterPLM v1 studies six ESM-2-8M layers with 10,420 dictionary features each, while above that scope effects on docking quality or interface-hypothesis stability remain unknown: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.12101v1.
items.sequential: Using frozen dictionaries, each intervention requires six baseline transformer layers followed by SAE manipulation and downstream layers, roughly fourteen stages uncached; proposed audit needs eight monomer-input slots × (baseline + reconstruction control + F interventions + F random controls), with unknown GPU busy fraction per run. Layers remain ordered, but cached activations permit concurrent intervention branches if memory and batching throughput suffice; nearest causal precedent is InterPLM steering, which does not measure this branching optimization: https://arxiv.org/html/2412.12101v1.
items.narrowing: Neural feature effects probe learned biological representations, not MEGADOCK mechanisms; useful for independently testable follow-up hypotheses.

items.title: Denser rigid-body search: recovery versus ranking
items.summary: Test whether added angular search improves rank1 and best50 DockQ under common workflow budgets; MEGADOCK documents 3,600 standard rotations and 54,000 dense rotations (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.root_link: Directly bears on GPU-dense minus GPU-standard rank1 and best50 DockQ under sealed budgets (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).
items.compute_open: More parallel compute buys search width: largest documented angular search in cited guide is 54,000 rotations; guide supplies settings rather than quality-scaling measurements, leaving whether denser coverage improves either DockQ outcome unknown here (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.sequential: none: rotation calculations parallelize through OpenMP and docking jobs distribute through MPI; angles need no preceding angle's result, although decoy reconstruction waits for docking output (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.narrowing: Leaves protocol repair and numerical acceptance aside; search-width response probes root's added-search value while retaining separate rank1/best50 outcomes (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).

items.title: Fixed-search docking throughput
items.summary: Developer benchmark reports 352 dockings taking 67.1 hours on one CPU core, 2.26 hours with 12 CPU cores plus one GPU, and 1.02 hours with 12 CPU cores plus three GPUs (https://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/perform.html).
items.root_link: Bears on CPU-standard/GPU-standard acceleration, whose complete-workflow timing boundary exceeds published docking timings (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md; https://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/perform.html).
items.compute_open: settled: parallel hardware reduced reported docking workload time from 67.1 hours on one CPU core to 1.02 hours on 12 CPU cores plus three GPUs, establishing compute sensitivity for that benchmark (https://www.bi.cs.titech.ac.jp/megadock/perform.html).
items.sequential: none: independent docking jobs distribute through MPI and rotations parallelize through OpenMP; downstream decoy generation waits for docking output (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/akiyamalab/MEGADOCK/master/doc/README.md).
items.narrowing: Leaves search quality and scientific agreement aside; docking time contributes to root's complete-workflow time but cannot establish its full acceleration ratio (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).

items.title: Massive multimer sampling and long recycling
items.summary: AFsample generated approximately 6,000 models per target and raised mean DockQ from 0.41 to 0.55 against its AlphaFold-Multimer baseline, while retaining confidently wrong orientations for T1187o (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10534052/).
items.root_link: Bears on finding good candidate poses versus ranking them first through an alternative method outside root's MEGADOCK arms (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).
items.compute_open: More parallel compute buys model runs/seeds: largest per-target sample count reported across cited studies is approximately 6,000; whether larger ensembles improve selected rank1 or best50 rather than candidate availability remains unestablished by them (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10534052/; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11578886/).
items.sequential: Each recycle waits for preceding prediction state; MassiveFold reports one prediction stopping at recycle 164 under a 1,000-recycle cap, while AFsample used approximately 6,000 separate predictions; scheduling reaches one prediction per GPU, but measured per-run GPU busy fraction is unreported (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11578886/; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10534052/). Recycles remain ordered under that recurrence; independent seeds can run concurrently given sufficient GPU resources, as MassiveFold demonstrated, shortening ensemble completion without removing one seed's dependency chain (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11578886/).
items.narrowing: Leaves identical docking inputs and backend equivalence aside; complex-prediction DockQ probes root's distinction between candidate coverage and selection (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).

items.title: GPU molecular dynamics for native-interface recovery
items.summary: Association study compared 16 ordinary MD runs with one coupled 16-replica exchange simulation per complex; exchange sampled near-native arrangements in five of six cases, leaving 1gcq unresolved after 640 ns per replica (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jcc.26187).
items.root_link: Bears on added-search pose recovery through molecular simulation outside root's rigid-body docking arms (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md).
items.compute_open: More parallel compute buys independent association seeds/ensemble members: cited association experiment used 16 ordinary trajectories or 16 coupled exchange replicas, reaching 899 ns ordinary and 845 ns per exchange replica; whether additional independent ensembles resolve remaining failures or reproduce force-field-favored wrong orientations remains unknown (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jcc.26187).
items.sequential: Each integration update waits for preceding positions/velocities and forces; proposed 2-fs steps imply roughly 154–450 million updates for reported 308–899-ns ordinary runs; benchmark used 16 independent ordinary runs or one coupled 16-replica exchange run per pair without establishing sufficient runs for convergence, and reports pmemd.cuda execution without per-run GPU busy fraction or original timestep in main text (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jcc.26187). Updates remain ordered in ordinary integration; coarse prediction plus concurrent fine corrections could overlap trajectory segments if an inexpensive coarse force field preserves relevant dynamics and converges cheaply—nearest cited physical demonstration applied adaptive Parareal to tungsten defects, leaving protein-association performance untested there (https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.10508).
items.narrowing: Leaves fixed MEGADOCK scoring and numerical agreement aside; near-native interface recovery provides a geometric proxy requiring validation against root's DockQ endpoints (file:///home/hal/dev/interp/metis/experiments/blind-02/20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/framer.md; https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/jcc.26187).
